category: Google Drive sharing front end and Drive manager (Indian DDL ecosystem)

free_tier.stated: "UNLIMITED - No quota limit. No annoying waiting times, Share & Download as many files as you want." Sharing and downloading are free and need no account.
free_tier.notes: The unlimited claim covers the sharing front end. The bytes remain on Google Drive, where the quota the page promises does not exist, does exist.

per_object_cap.stated: Not stated on the site. The only size-shaped statement is that the service plays and shares video stored in the owner's Drive.
per_object_cap.notes: Drive's own per-file limits apply and are not restated.

retention.stated: Not stated for the links. The about page claims 'New Layers of Backup Drive System Added to Keep Files Alive', which is about the operator's re-upload behaviour, not a retention promise to a user.

egress.terms: Downloads are served by the site as one-click links, 'No annoying waiting times'. No allowance, price or meter is printed.

interface_detail: Web only as read: a dashboard, 'Sign in using Google+' OAuth, drive browsing, bulk link export, and a documented 'Download Folder Change Option' in the profile panel. No API, RSS or CLI was found on the pages read.
tooling: Third-party bypass scripts exist for the whole family (bypasser.py in Link-Bypasser-Bot lists driveseed among the gdlist hosts), which is the de-facto API. No first-party client.
chaining: The last wrapper before the bytes: an index site posts a DriveSeed link, the downloader lands on a Google-hosted file, and the link survives re-uploads because the operator keeps backup Drives. It sits behind FilePress and HubCloud in the same chain and is interchangeable with GDFlix, which ships the same page.

limits.value: unstated; the Drive-side per-file throttle is inherited

limits_note: The about page's own changelog names the constraint the marketing hides: '403: User Rate Limit Exceeded - Fixed to Great Extent'. The phrase 'to great extent' is the operator admitting the fix is partial.
binding_note: A client pulling 1 TiB a month through DriveSeed pulls it from Google, and Google's per-file and per-session shaping is what stops the transfer. The site adds no counter that could bind first.

identity_cost.detail: Downloading needs nothing. Publishing or managing a Drive needs Google OAuth with drive scope: 'You have to Sign Up through google and allow our application the Permissions to access and manage your google drive.'

reliability_note: The service is a Google OAuth app holding drive scope over the user's account, so a publisher's exposure is the whole Drive, not one folder. Links depend on the operator's backup Drives staying alive, and the site has rotated versions (v5.1 today, with a 'Fully New Dark Theme' rewrite) without a stable public changelog.
confidence_note: Homepage and about page read on the live host. The 'unlimited' claim is the vendor's, unmeasured: no download was pulled and no quota was seen to fail. What would raise the rung is one scripted fetch of a large shared file with the byte count and the throttle status.

evidence.proved: live at v5.1 with the 'UNLIMITED - No quota limit' claim, 'Sign in using Google+', TeamDrive support and a share-link flow

the Drive-manager model ('allow our application the Permissions to access and manage your google drive'), the quota framing ('without worrying about quota limits reached'), and the changelog line '403: User Rate Limit Exceeded - Fixed to Great Extent'
driveseed is listed in a maintained bypass script's gdlist alongside gdflix, hubdrive and drivehub, so the family is automated by third parties rather than by an API

extras.template_twin: gdflix (v4.6) serves the same copy and layout
